history.period: Original Margao temple pre-Portuguese; deities shifted to Zambaulim 1565-1567
history.summary: The celebrated Shiva-as-Damodar temple on the bank of the Kushawati river at Zambaulim. The deity originally stood at Mathagam (Margao), where the Holy Spirit Church now stands; during the Portuguese temple-destruction campaign in Salcete (1567) the Mahajans of Margao shifted Damodar along with Ramnath, Laxmi-Narayan, Chamundeshwari, Mahakali and Mahesh to Zambaulim, where the Desais of Rivona granted land (vatan still paid). Local tradition also links the shrine to Makaji Damodar of Margao. The temple belongs to the Gowda Saraswat Brahmin (GSB) community, has accommodation in its complex, and is revered by Hindus and Catholics alike (the deity is fondly called 'Dambab'); the Kushawati is believed to have healing powers. town_description: Zambaulim is a village in Quepem taluka, South Goa, on the banks of the Kushawati river about 22 km from Margao and 5 km from Quepem town, near the Sanguem border.
